- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is positive (especially >0.5) — model tends to overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate when sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment <0.25) — model fails to capture downside risk or bearish momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., >70) — model often peaks too early and then overcorrects downward.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias — model frequently forecasts a return to prior mean after a spike, but true price often continues trending.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts slowly to sentiment changes, especially when sentiment turns negative.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too low in the first 5–7 days, then rise sharply — model underestimates initial momentum.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model tends to overforecast the peak — then undercorrects later.
- Avoid averaging sentiment across all days — focus on recent sentiment (last 3–5 days) for correction, as it better reflects current market direction.
